items.title: A failure before any mutation ends as 96 (not launched), not as 98 with a session-wide lock
items.spec:
Evidence: Core.ps1:454-459 maps any $Failure to 98. Then Core.ps1:494-496 calls Stop-PestoQueueRemainingForSafety, which sets $script:MutationUncertain (Core.ps1:3594). The unit path already returns 96 in this case (Direct.ps1:431-438).
Change Complete-PestoQueueItem (Core.ps1:449-501). When $Failure is set and $ticket.Monitor is not null, read Monitor.MutationStarted and Monitor.TimedOut under a lock on Monitor.SyncRoot. If both are false and neither the exception nor its InnerException is a TimeoutException, set code 96 with the message 'Action non lancée : <cause>. Aucune commande Windows ou AD engagée.'
Keep the existing codes for: TimeoutException (97), MutationStarted=true (98), Monitor null (98), unknown code (98).
Add Stop-PestoQueueRemainingNotStarted. It runs the same loop as Stop-PestoQueueRemainingForSafety: remaining rows get 'NON LANCÉ', Traiter=$false, CancelCount++. It must NOT set $script:MutationUncertain, and it saves the checkpoint with phase 'Idle'. On this 96 path, call it, then Complete-PestoQueueRun.
Fail-PestoQueueCallback stays 98. Do not touch receipts: a central receipt already written with phase 'Running' keeps blocking its target through Test-PestoInterventionConflict.
items.tests:
Mac, pwsh 7.4.20: AST-extract Complete-PestoQueueItem and the new stop function. Stub Set-PestoQueueRowResult, Add-LogLine, Write-AuditLine, Sync-Grid, Save-PestoQueueCheckpointSafe, Request-PestoQueuePump and Complete-PestoQueueRun, and use a synchronized-hashtable monitor. Cases:
(a) Failure with MutationStarted=false gives 96, MutationUncertain stays false, and the remaining rows become 'NON LANCÉ'.
(b) MutationStarted=true gives 98 and MutationUncertain=true.
(c) TimeoutException gives 97.
(d) TimedOut=true never gives 96.
(e) A null monitor gives 98.
Windows, later: Stabilisation and QueueRemoval suites. On a VM copy with ActiveDirectory.psd1 renamed, check that the next queue run can still be launched.

items.title: Import: header mapping ignores case, and a non-UTF-8 file gets a clear instruction
items.spec:
Evidence:
- BatchTools.ps1:99: `-in` matches headers ignoring case but stores the target spelling.
- BatchTools.ps1:37: [Array]::IndexOf is case-sensitive and returns -1, so a cell silently becomes 'false' or ''.
- BatchTools.ps1:95: Get-Item checks the size, then ReadAllText decodes strictly with no catch, so the user sees a raw DecoderFallbackException.
Changes:
(1) Add a pure Resolve-PestoImportAutoMapping -Headers -Targets. It returns a hashtable from each target to the exact header string (first OrdinalIgnoreCase match). Show-PestoMappedImport uses it and prompts only for targets with no match.
(2) New-PestoImportEditor resolves each mapped header ignoring case. If a mapping value is non-empty and matches no header, throw 'Colonne associée introuvable : <nom>. Aucune ligne ajoutée.' An unmapped value ('') keeps today's defaults: 'false' for Renommer and Deplacer, '' otherwise. Rows stay unchecked, with NeedsReview and 'À CONTRÔLER'.
(3) Extract Read-PestoImportFile -Path. It calls Assert-PestoPlainPath, checks FileInfo.Length <= 8 MiB before reading, calls ReadAllBytes once, strips the UTF-8 BOM and decodes strictly. On DecoderFallbackException it throws 'Fichier non UTF-8. Dans Excel, choisissez « CSV UTF-8 (délimité par des virgules) », puis importez de nouveau. Aucune ligne ajoutée.' Do not fall back to ANSI.
items.tests:
Mac, pwsh, Run-BatchNames120Tests:
- Lowercase headers map without a prompt: Renommer cell 'true', Nom_du_PC 'PC1'.
- A mapping to a missing header throws the French message.
- A cp1252 file gives the instruction message.
- Files with and without a BOM give identical text.
- A file of 8 MiB + 1 byte is refused before it is read.
Windows, later: import an Excel ANSI file and a lowercase-header CSV in the GUI.

items.title: Compute the queue content stamp without recursive hashing
items.spec:
Evidence: Get-PestoQueueContentStamp (BatchTools.ps1:59-63) runs Get-PestoStableHash, a recursive function followed by ConvertTo-Json, on every row. It was measured at 515 ms per 1 000 rows under pwsh 7, and it is called 3 to 5 times per import, multi-edit or undo (BatchTools.ps1:69, 76, 80, 86, 106, 114-115, 121).
Rewrite it with a StringBuilder:
- First, the ordered column names and their types.
- Then, for each row and each ItemArray cell, a typed, length-prefixed token: DBNull 'N;', bool 'B1;' or 'B0;', string 'S<len>:<v>;', any other value 'V<len>:<Convert.ToString(v,[Globalization.CultureInfo]::InvariantCulture)>;'.
- Rows are separated by a newline.
Hash with SHA256 and return lowercase hex. Stamps are only compared within one session, so the format may change. Callers stay unchanged.
items.tests:
Mac, pwsh:
- A table and its .Copy() give the same stamp.
- The stamp changes when a single cell changes (string; bool; '' versus DBNull; 'True' string versus True bool), when the row order changes, and when a column is added.
- Existing undo, publish and refusal cases still pass. Update the AST load lists if Get-PestoStableHash is no longer needed.
- 5 000 rows take under 500 ms in pwsh 7.

items.title: Explicit relaunch through the existing UAC relay ('Relancer Pesto' after settings; relaunch with an AD account)

(2) Startup, route Elevate:

Delete it, then call Invoke-PestoStartupElevation again with the same parameters (+ -AskCredential for 76; + the profile's ConfigPath, see the profiles item).

(3) Core side:
- Get-PestoRelaunchOffer -CfgRestartRequired -NeedsExplicitCredential returns {Mode, Label, Allowed, Reason}. Allowed is false when not relayed (launched already elevated, Consult, Demo), with Reason 'Relancez Pesto manuellement'.

Aucun mot de passe n''est conservé.', write the request with Write-PestoAtomicText, set $script:PestoRelaunchExitCode, and close $Win through the normal Closing path (queue checkpoint saved).
